mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.25% signals a highly accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and encouraging risk-taking, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2% annualized growth signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% annualized and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3% within a month, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 1% YoY and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth is below 1% YoY and UNRATE rises by more than 0.3% in a month.
